newsitem.title: USA: The biggest boom in modern retailing: Books.
newsitem.headline: The biggest boom in modern retailing: Books.

text.p: Despite the fear that television would change America into a nation of illiterates, the biggest gains in the modern era of retailing have been made by book stores.

Of all retailing formats, book stores racked up the biggest gain -- 329 percent since 1975 -- in findings by research firm Audits & Surveys Worldwide, which based its survey on a national sample of 35,000 retail outlets in 800 geographic areas.

Whether a sign of a literary renaissance or entreprenerial fervor, book stores have flourished over recent decades, even though growth limits have been hit more recently. The total number of book stores has fallen 3 percent in the 1990s, a modest drop probably due to direct competition with one another.
As in other retailing formats, independents succumbed to superstore operators.

But big chains have been able to withstand the competition of warehouse clubs and discounters by offering bigger and wider lists of titles at discounts, as well as chairs to sit and read and sip gourmet coffee.

In another sign that reading is alive and well, a proliferation of magazine titles has helped news dealers and newstands to survive the long-term decline in newspaper readership and grow 82 percent since 1970. They have risen 3 percent alone in 1996 over 1995 to a total of 9,760.

Other telltale signs about popular culture are seen in the fate of retailing formats. Barber shops have declined 14 percent in the last five years to 41,340, the number of beauty shops rose 8 percent to an impressive 210,590. Reason: many beauty shops are unisex in practice, thus drawing both male and female customers.
Other big gainers include camera and photo supply stores, up 39.4 percent since 1975 to 4,910; and jewelry stores, up 81.9 percent since 1970 to 39,130.

Liquor stores are up 30 percent to 41,960 despite a drop in liquor consumption overall -- as fine wine and microbeers spurred home-based drinking. But a nationwide trend toward fitness is still in full bloom: sporting goods stores are up a staggering 160 percent to 37,580 since 1975.
